Logan —
See a first pass below (I’ll attach a clean Appendix and the eval workbook by EOD). High-level: we treat inference surfaces as production systems with a layered approach: runtime protections, QA/eval pipelines pre-release, and monitoring & rollback post-release.

1) NIST AI RMF mapping (summary)
- Govern: Compliance & policy controls via private deployment, role-based access (RBAC), and customer-configurable data retention.
- Map: Model/component inventory, pinned versions, and metadata tagging for provenance.
- Measure: Continuous metrics (latency, token-level errors, QA score distributions, fairness metrics) and automated eval runs.
- Manage: Canary rollouts, automatic fallback to smaller-mode or deterministic templates, and KV/prefix cache invalidation processes.

2) Eval & regression approach (summary)
- Pre-release: unitized prompt tests, targeted slice tests (demographics, edge cases), synthetic adversarial prompts, and acceptance gates based on calibration & bias thresholds.
- Post-release monitoring: drift detection via embedding distribution shifts + task-specific metric decay, weekly regression suites, and alerting tied to SLA/quality thresholds.
- Release gating: block releases on threshold regressions; automatic rollback and hotfix flow.

I’m attaching a sample workbook with: baseline metrics definitions, regression test matrix, and an example runbook for an observed calibration drift.

Attachments (to include): Redwood_Eval_Regimen.xlsx (sample), Redwood_RFP_Appendix_NIST_mapping.pdf (draft).

-Marissa
Sr. Product Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Team — quick legal/compliance notes for the EU AI Act section. Short version: Northbridge’s described use (credit-decision assistance + customer messaging) will likely be interpreted as a high-risk use case where the bank is the controller and Redwood is a provider of a component/service. Our recommended posture:

- Classification: Treat the engagements as "high-risk" for EU AI Act purposes. We should be clear we are a provider of an AI component and outline responsibilities for the customer (data labeling, final human oversight).
- Technical mitigations we will commit to in the RFP:
  - Human oversight configurations (explicit HMI/approval controls and logs).
  - Explainability artifacts for decisioning models (model cards + salient feature summaries).
  - Logging & retention policy: per-customer audit log exports and schema (timestamp, model_version, prompt_hash, response_hash, confidence_score, decision_flag).
  - Risk assessment template (we provide a starting RA that Northbridge can customize).
- Evidence: we can provide SOC2 Type II summary (redacted), sample audit log schema, and a sanitized eval run (no PII).

One legal caveat: for a fully managed hosted deployment where we host customer data, customers may need to run separate DPIA (data protection impact assessment). If they insist on us being the processor for high-risk decisioning, we should recommend Dedicated or Private deployment and include contractual SLAs & subprocessors list.

I’ll draft the EU AI Act positioning paragraph and a short mitigation checklist for the appendix.

-Neha
Head of Legal & Compliance
Redwood Inference
